CD Projekt’s Best Days May Be Ahead

Weekly Digest
CD Projekt’s Best Days May Be Ahead
By Naavik •   October 11, 2026
Source: CD Projekt Red
CD Projekt develops and publishes premium role-playing games (RPGs) as well as licenses its franchises to commercial partners like Netflix. For most of its history, it has moved from one enormous production to the next. The Witcher 3 arrived in 2015, Cyberpunk 2077 followed in 2020, and its Phantom Liberty expansion came three years later. The next announced standalone flagship, The Witcher 4, is targeted for 2028. That leaves the company with a familiar question: what supports the business while one flagship absorbs years of work? Or as joint CEO Michał Nowakowski framed the goal in a
recent interview
: “how can we do more, but not compromise on quality?”
Part of the answer is that CD Projekt now has more of its studio moving in parallel.
The Witcher 4 is in full production
, Cyberpunk 2 is in pre-production within a growing North American organization, and several smaller or partner-led projects sit around them. CD Projekt still heavily depends on blockbusters, but it is trying harder to make each one a foundation for later releases while another franchise advances alongside it.
So far the transition has been well managed, in part because its mature games still sell well. The company generated
PLN 435M ($120M) in revenue and PLN 249M ($68M) in net profit
in the first half of 2026, even without a major new release. CD Projekt’s first-half revenue has risen every year since 2023, while its net margin climbed from 37% to 57%, even though the company has not launched another standalone blockbuster during this period.
Source:
CD Projekt H1 2026 investor presentation
Most recently, existing Cyberpunk and Witcher products have supplied most of the revenue, while licensing and partnerships have contributed nearly PLN 95M ($26M). That latter contribution includes undisclosed initiatives, but it reflects the broader effort to keep its franchises commercially active. For example,
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 is scheduled to return to Netflix
later this month, and it’s important to remember that the first season
led to a spike in players
of Cyberpunk 2077 back in 2022. A new, live-action
Cyberpunk movie
with Paramount was also just announced.
At the same time, the company invested roughly PLN 385M ($106M) in new development work (through capitalized project expenditures) during the half and ended June with about PLN 1.29B ($341M) across cash, deposits, and bonds. That cash flow and cash hoard cushion give CD Projekt more flexibility to invest in overlapping projects.
Building Two Flagship Teams
The clearest evidence of organizational change is that Cyberpunk 2 is advancing before the next Witcher game is finished. Its allocation rose from 84 developers in February 2025 to 184 by July 2026, including 21 additions between April and July. Shared services added another 23 people over those three months, while The Witcher 4 remained near 500 developers.
Source:
CD Projekt H1 2026 investor presentation
Yes, these games are at different stages, but even so, Cyberpunk 2 having 35% of the staff size of The Witcher 4 as the latter nears peak production is a real change of pace from the past. It’s not an entirely new way of operating — CD Projekt developed Phantom Liberty while early work on The Witcher 4 was underway — but this represents a bigger jump since Phantom Liberty wasn’t a standalone production and was built with an established technical base.
Cyberpunk 2 is being developed across studios in Boston, Vancouver, and Poland, alongside remote staff. Consequently, CD Projekt’s North American presence is evolving far beyond a simple satellite branch (which contrasts with the broader move away from North American development elsewhere in the industry). According to a
company interview with an engineering director
, three directors divide core responsibilities and map cross-location interdisciplinary dependencies.
In tandem with these organizational shifts, CD Projekt is transitioning its upcoming portfolio from REDengine (its proprietary technology) to Unreal Engine 5. Previously, the company coupled game design with ongoing iteration of its REDengine, requiring significant additional manpower and time to get both ready for production. By adopting Unreal Engine as a unified foundation, the studio can more easily transfer tools, engineering expertise, and talent across teams, enabling faster speed of development. Of course, this migration does not instantly streamline production. CD Projekt must construct customized internal pipelines on top of the engine, and hundreds of staff members have had to adapt to a new technical environment. However, in the long run, betting on a best-in-class engine that enables superior technology reuse and greater focus on design should provide upside that’s worth the pain of transitioning.
Taken together, superior financial footing, an engine reset, and a growing team that’s split across parallel AAA projects have laid the groundwork for CD Projekt to expand and accelerate its release schedule without creating new development bottlenecks.
Expanding Into the Future
Source:
CD Projekt H1 investor presentation
Although management does not appear to be rushing The Witcher 4, it has
repeatedly said it aims to release all three games in the new Witcher trilogy within six years beginning with The Witcher 4
. It has not published dates for the next two games, and according to joint CEO Nowakowski “it would be difficult for us to add an expansion to the upcoming trilogy.” This acceleration, despite low DLC hopes, is perhaps aggressive, but it is in part made more realistic by the shift to Unreal, enabling the future team to reuse The Witcher 4’s technology, assets, and pipelines.
